steps.t: Sit down and let the chair take your weight.
Keep the eyes open, with a soft gaze.
Point at something in front of you — a wall, a cup, a window.
Now turn the finger around, and point at the place where others would see your face.
Looking now, not from memory — is there a face here, or open space?
Thoughts will arrive. Treat them as trains. You can watch them pass without boarding.
If you already got on one, notice that. Step back onto the platform.
Rest as the space this is all happening in.
When you stand, stand as the same space.
Sit so you can forget the sitting. Eyes open.
Point out at a thing. See it clearly — color, shape, distance.
Now point back at where others see your face.
What is here, on this side of the finger?
The world is there. Space is here. Both at once.
Let a thought pass through that space. Do not follow it.
Check again. Still no face?
Rest as that.
Sit easy. Eyes can close, or stay softly open.
Is it possible to imagine the space between your eyes?
The space between your ears.
The space inside the mouth, and the throat.
Now the space around the body — behind you, above you, below the seat.
See if inside and outside can be one continuous space.
Rest in that. Diffuse is enough.
Sit or lie down. Close the mouth. Breathe through the nose.
Let the breath be light. This is not a performance.
A little slower, only if that is easy.
If the mind runs, let it. Keep the nose breathing.
Stay with the next breath only.
That is the whole practice.
Sit. Eyes open. Leave the view as it is.
There is already knowing here. You do not have to make it.
A thought appears. Let it be a thought. Do not follow, do not fight.
Rest as the knowing in which the thought appeared.
If you get involved, notice that. That noticing is the same knowing.
Leave it. Already awake is not a future state.
Sit upright, at ease. Eyes open or barely so.
Turn attention around, as if mind were looking at mind.
What does mind look like, when you look directly?
If you find no thing there, do not fill the gap. Leave it.
Thoughts can move. Mind remains unstained, like space.
Rest. Do not meddle.
Sit upright. Not stiff. Awake.
Eyes lowered. Soft gaze on the floor ahead.
This is the practice. Nothing extra.
A thought arrives. Open the hand of thought. Let it go.
Return is not a failure. Return is the practice.
Just sit.
Sit. Let the body be quiet.
A thought is here. Ask, gently: who is this appearing to?
Do not answer with a name, or a story. Look.
Whatever you find — or fail to find — stay with that.
The one who would finish this practice is another thought.
Rest as what does not come and go.
Sit still. Eyes closed if that helps.
Feel the breath at the nostrils, or the belly. That is the home base.
When a thought pulls you, note it — thinking — and return.
When a sound appears, note hearing, and return.
You are not trying to stop anything. You are seeing it change.
Keep returning. That is the practice.
Sit comfortably. Close the eyes.
Rest attention on the breath, wherever it is easiest to feel.
When you wander, come back. No commentary.
The breath does not need to be special. Ordinary breathing is the object.
Stay. Return. Stay.
Sit easy. Soften the face.
Bring to mind yourself, as you are right now. Not the improved version.
Quietly: may I be safe. May I be at ease.
If that feels false, do not force it. Offer the wish anyway, like setting a cup down.
Now someone easy to care for. May you be safe. May you be at ease.
Let that be enough.
Sit. Close the eyes if you like.
Notice who is here. A worried part, a driven part, a tired part. Do not pick a fight.
Ask, inwardly: how old does this part feel? Then wait.
You are not the part. You are the space it is appearing in.
Thank it for trying to help. You can drive from the platform.
Rest as that wider space.
Sit or stand. Mouth closed. Breathe in through the nose.
On the next out-breath, hum a single easy tone. Not loud. Just a hum.
Again. In through the nose. Hum on the way out. Let the chest and face vibrate.
If a thought comes, let the tone hold you instead of the thought.
Keep humming. I will be quiet while you do.
Stop. Feel the silence after the sound.
Sit. Choose one simple sound. Ah, om, or a word you already use.
On the out-breath, say it. Out loud if you can, or under the breath.
Again. Same sound. No melody required.
Let the sound carry the attention. You do not have to think the sound.
Continue. I will be quiet.
Stop. Hear the room.
Lie down, or sit. Close the eyes if that helps.
Feel the feet. No need to change them. Just the sensation.
Feel the lower legs, the knees, the thighs.
Belly, chest, the small movement of breathing.
Feel the hands, the arms, the shoulders, the face.
The whole body as one field of sensation. Rest there.
Stand. Phone away. Eyes open.
Feel the weight in both feet.
Begin to walk, slower than usual. Heel, then sole, then toes.
When the mind leaves, it is not a problem. Come back to the next step.
Keep walking. The step is the sit.
Stop. Feel the standing. Then go on with the day.
Stand. Feel the floor.
Imagine a simple boundary around this place — a circle, a room, enough space to be in.
Look to one direction. See what is there. Then turn, and see the next.
Four directions, then back to the center. You are the space in the middle.
Rest as that center. Nothing to banish but distraction.
When you are done, the circle can go. The looking can stay.
Sit. You do not need to hold on to what happened.
If images or feelings are still here, let them be trains. Watch them pass.
Do not build a religion out of a state. States end.
What is here now, without the story of last night or last year?
Rest as the space those leftovers are moving through.
The ordinary day is the integration.
Sit. Pick one simple object — the breath, a sound, or a spot on the wall.
Rest attention there. When it leaves, you will notice. That noticing is the practice.
Return without a story about how you failed.
The object does not have to be interesting. Ordinary is better.
I will be quiet. Stay, wander, return.
Let the focus soften. The same attention can go wide.
Sit easy. Close the eyes.
Take a word you already use, or the word one. This is not a secret. It is a vehicle.
Think it easily, on the breath or off it. No force. No concentration contest.
If it fades, let it fade. If you remember it, pick it up again. Both are correct.
I will be quiet. Easy repetition. No managing.
Drop the word. Sit in what is already here.
Sit or lie down. Close the eyes.
Picture a simple room you know, just for a moment. Walls, light, a chair.
Now drop the picture. What remains is the seeing itself, even with eyes closed.
If the image comes back, let it. Then notice the space it appears in.
I will be quiet. Image or no image — same space.
Open the eyes. The room you are in is not a picture.
Sit or lie down. You can open your eyes or stop this at any time.
Feel the heaviness of the hands, the feet, the jaw.
Each out-breath, a little heavier, as if the chair were doing the work.
You are not going anywhere. You are still the space these sensations appear in.
I will be quiet. Heavy, and aware.
Wiggle the fingers. The heaviness can go. The awareness does not.
Stand, or sit if standing is not available. Eyes open.
Feel both feet. Begin a slow sway, as small as you like.
The movement is the sit. You do not have to freeze to be present.
When a thought boards, keep swaying. Come back to the next shift of weight.
I will be quiet. Slow movement. Eyes open.
Stillness now. Same space, not moving.
Sit or lie down. Never do this in water, or while driving. Stop if you feel dizzy.
Mouth or nose — take thirty somewhat stronger breaths. Full in, relaxed out.
After the last exhale, rest with empty lungs, only as long as it is easy.
A full breath in, hold a few seconds, then let it go. Ordinary breathing now.
Feel the body. You are the space this energy is happening in, not the storm.
That is one round. Enough.
Sit. Soft eyes.
This space you are sitting in is not private. The same awareness holds others too.
Wish, simply: may the one who suffers — including you — be free of the extra story.
Now look: the wisher is also an appearance in the same space.
I will be quiet. Open, and kind, without a project.
Carry both — space, and the wish — into the next conversation.
Sit. This is a map of attention, not a belief you have to join.
Imagine ten places on a tree, from the ground to a crown of space.
Rest for a moment at the crown — open, unoccupied, like the sky.
Descend to the heart. Warmth, if it is there. If not, space will do.
Return to the crown. Same you, two places, one looking.
Drop the map. The tree was a scaffold. The space remains.
